General.Description:
Norwegian glaciologist Sigrid Haas was eighteen hours into a routine ice-core sampling mission when the research station collapsed into a melt pond. She reached the surface with a GPS unit, a survival kit rated for seventy-two hours, and the knowledge that the nearest human settlement was three hundred and forty kilometres away across drifting sea ice.

What followed was twenty-two days of survival that Sigrid documented in a waterproof field notebook, writing in the margins of her data sheets when she had nothing else to write on. Arctic Drift is reconstructed from those notes, from satellite imagery of her path, and from Sigrid's own prodigious memory — tested and verified against meteorological records that confirm every detail she describes.

Maren Solberg is not writing a survival manual, though the knowledge Sigrid deploys is real and could save a life. She is writing about what happens to a mind that is alone, cold, and working at the absolute limits of its capacity day after day. About what you think about. About what turns out to matter.

Harrowing and deeply human. You will not put it down.
